Bundle all variants**\r\n\r\n- 4 regular weights + 2 monospace weights (400 and 700, as sometimes code is rendered bold)\r\n- 2 formats (`woff` + `woff2`)\r\n- 6 charsets\r\n\r\n= 48 font files. At least. The numbers in the linked comment are higher because I included more weights and charsets. Remember that Material for MkDocs is used in [50+ languages](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/changing-the-language/#configuration), so we cannot possibly loose support for some languages by removing some character sets, we need to support all of them to some degree.\r\n\r\n**2. Bundle woff/ttf including all charsets**\r\n\r\n`Roboto-Regular.ttf` weighs `164kb`. Take that times 6 (4 + 2 weights), you're at `984kb`. `woff` and `woff2` are possibly a little smaller than `ttf`, but not an order of magnitude. Currently, Material for MkDocs without fonts weighs `58kb` (gzipped), i.e. all CSS and JS sources. `woff` and `woff2` cannot be gzipped, as they're binary formats. Each font loaded from Google fonts adds `11kb` per font, so a total of around `66kb` for all fonts (for the regular `latin` charset), leading to:\r\n\r\n- `58kb` + `66kb` = `124kb` using Google Gonts\r\n- `58kb`+ `984kb` = `1042kb` using bundled `ttf` fonts\r\n\r\nThat's an order of magnitude, and only for Roboto, so you would be locked in to use this font.\r\n\r\n**Recommendation**\r\n\r\n[Turn font loading off](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/changing-the-fonts/#monospaced-font) and fall back to system fonts. If that's not an option, you can download the font files and [bundle them yourself](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/changing-the-fonts/#additional-fonts), but your website will likely receive worse scores on Lighthouse and/or Google.\r\n\r\n**Personal opinion**\r\n\r\nThis ruling is pretty interesting because it would mean that all use of CDNs without the visitor's consent could be considered \"leaking the visitors IP\", at least as I read it. <p dir="auto">As in EU the GDPR starts to be active from May 25th on. It would be good if all external fonts and services are part of the bundle and do not link to the CDN version. Otherwise we have to display a cookie consent and a privacy policy for a "documentation".</p>
<h3 dir="auto">Expected behavior</h3>
<p dir="auto">Please include the Material Icons and Roboto Font directly (and other external services) into the bundle at least everything which is needed for the default material theme.<br>
Currently it is not GDPR compliant how it is right now.</p>
<h3 dir="auto">Actual behavior</h3>
<p dir="auto">It's loaded from a CDN.</p>
<h3 dir="auto">Steps to reproduce the bug</h3>
<p dir="auto">In the Base.html (maybe in other files as well) from the material design there are links to the CDN services.</p></div></div><div class="IssueBodyTaskList__-FlQre"><div role="toolbar" </li>

href="https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/browser-support/" rel="nofollow">all browsers currently supported</a>? I believe it would involve 5 font files of total ~240KB. Including <code class="notranslate">woff</code> as well would make it a total of 10 font files and ~540KB.</p>
<p dir="auto">It appears <code class="notranslate">woff2</code> is currently supported by <a href="https://caniuse.com/woff2" rel="nofollow">~94.9%</a> of user's browsers, with <code class="notranslate">woff</code> at <a href="https://caniuse.com/woff" rel="nofollow">96.7%</a>.</p>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://google-webfonts-helper.herokuapp.com/fonts/roboto?subsets=cyrillic,cyrillic-ext,greek,greek-ext,latin,latin-ext,vietnamese" rel="nofollow">Roboto</a>, <a href="https://google-webfonts-helper.herokuapp.com/fonts/roboto-mono?subsets=cyrillic,cyrillic-ext,greek,latin,latin-ext,vietnamese" rel="nofollow">Roboto Mono</a> (note the 'Modern Browsers' option).</p>
<p dir="auto">Only reason I'm mentioning that is, it's much more practical than the previously mentioned bundling of 105 font files and their corresponding CSS. I understand that the browsers you support has probably modernised since 2018 and that's likely why we can get away with only 1 or 2 font formats now, that and the combining of multiple charsets into a single font file.</p>
<p dir="auto">I would understand if you still preferred not to bundle these, as I know it would be another dependency when building (although updates to <a href="https://github.com/googlefonts/roboto">the font itself</a> are infrequent), and the increase of either 240KB or 540KB for the project. Another aspect is the request from the browser itself to the web server will now be asking for more data directly, whereas it would have got a quick CDN or browser cache hit if using Google href="https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-396045729">#739 (comment)</a>. You would have two options.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>1. Bundle all variants</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>4 regular weights + 2 monospace weights (400 and 700, as sometimes code is rendered bold)</li>
<li>2 formats (<code class="notranslate">woff</code> + <code class="notranslate">woff2</code>)</li>
<li>6 charsets</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">= 48 font files. At least. The numbers in the linked comment are higher because I included more weights and charsets. Remember that Material for MkDocs is used in <a href="https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/changing-the-language/#configuration" rel="nofollow">50+ languages</a>, so we cannot possibly loose support for some languages by removing some character sets, we need to support all of them to some degree.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>2. Bundle woff/ttf including all charsets</strong></p>
<p dir="auto"><code class="notranslate">Roboto-Regular.ttf</code> weighs <code class="notranslate">164kb</code>. Take that times 6 (4 + 2 weights), you're at <code class="notranslate">984kb</code>. <code class="notranslate">woff</code> and <code class="notranslate">woff2</code> are possibly a little smaller than <code class="notranslate">ttf</code>, but not an order of magnitude. Currently, Material for MkDocs without fonts weighs <code class="notranslate">58kb</code> (gzipped), i.e. all CSS and JS sources. <code class="notranslate">woff</code> and <code class="notranslate">woff2</code> cannot be gzipped, as they're binary formats. Each font loaded from Google fonts adds <code class="notranslate">11kb</code> per font, so a total of around <code class="notranslate">66kb</code> for all fonts (for the regular <code class="notranslate">latin</code> charset), leading to:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code class="notranslate">58kb</code> + <code class="notranslate">66kb</code> = <code class="notranslate">124kb</code> using Google Gonts</li>
<li><code class="notranslate">58kb</code>+ <code class="notranslate">984kb</code> = <code class="notranslate">1042kb</code> using bundled <code class="notranslate">ttf</code> fonts</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">That's an order of magnitude, and only for Roboto, so you would be locked in to use this font.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Recommendation</strong></p>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/changing-the-fonts/#monospaced-font" rel="nofollow">Turn font loading off</a> and fall back to system fonts. If that's not an option, you can download the font files and <a href="https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/changing-the-fonts/#additional-fonts" rel="nofollow">bundle them yourself</a>, but your website will likely receive worse scores on Lighthouse and/or Google.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Personal opinion</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">This ruling is pretty interesting because it would mean that all use of CDNs without the visitor's consent could be considered "leaking the visitors IP", at least as I read it. Thus, all use of external assets (not services, assets!), be it from third-party cookie consent providers, analytics integrations, etc., basically, everything hosted on external servers must be considered problematic at least. I believe that this ruling will not be persistent. Thus, I would be patient and wait for how this is handled.</p>
<p dir="auto">Note that this is my personal opinion and I'm not an expert in legal affairs, but it might help to understand my argument.</p>

<blockquote>

I believe that this ruling will not be persistent. Thus, I would be patient and wait for how this is handled.</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">As I already wrote in 2018, this ruling was to be expected and is a natural consequence of BDSG (2006) and GDPR (2016). </blockquote>
<p dir="auto">Correct. Please refer to <a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="306569468" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739/hovercard?comment_id=1027713955&comment_type=issue_comment" href="https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/739#issuecomment-1027713955">#739 (comment)</a> to understand why it's (currently) not an option.</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto">And considering <a href="https://www.cnil.fr/en/use-google-analytics-and-data-transfers-united-states-cnil-orders-website-manageroperator-comply" rel="nofollow">France</a> and the Netherlands now have also followed Austria and declared use of third-party services or assets without manual consent illegal, so you shouldn’t expect this to change soon (and should instead provide an option where mkdocs downloads the required fonts during build time, potentially even subsetting only the required parts depending on which text is actually used in the project)</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">You're invited to create a PR. If you manage to pull this off, I'm happy to merge it. However, doing this during build time would mean that we would need to implement this as part of a plugin (otherwise we cannot hook into the build process), in order to pull out the glyphs for the configured language(s). I suspect that it's significantly more complicated than just switching off the fonts and falling back to system fonts.</p>
<p dir="auto">If you wish to include Roboto yourself, it's not complicated at all. You don't even need theme extension – just add a custom CSS file, a <code class="notranslate">@font-face</code> definition and put the relevant <code class="notranslate">*.woff</code> files into your <code class="notranslate">assets</code> folder.</p>
<p dir="auto">If you don't wish to do it, you're free to use any other static site generator you like.</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap"><div <ol dir="auto">
<li>Select the character sets you really need</li>
<li>Select styles 300, 400, 400i and 700</li>
<li>Copy the CSS and <a href="https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/changing-the-fonts/#additional-fonts" rel="nofollow">add it in an additional stylesheet</a></li>
<li>Download the fonts and put them in your <code class="notranslate">docs_dir</code> relative to the CSS file</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Repeat for the monospaced font with the weights you need (probably 400 and 700)</p>
<p dir="auto"><del>Sadly, this is a manual process and not automatable. data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto"><strong>Insiders 4.9.0</strong> adds a new plugin: the <a href="https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/ensuring-data-privacy/" rel="nofollow"><strong>built-in privacy plugin</strong></a> – the plugin will automatically download all external scripts, style and web fonts, so you can self-host them as part of your documentation without manual effort. The idea is to make compliance with GDPR easier, given the latest developments when serving external assets to users without prior consent.</p>
<p dir="auto">Activate it via <code class="notranslate">mkdocs.yml</code> with:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-yaml notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="plugins:
  - privacy"><pre class="notranslate"><span class="pl-ent">plugins</span>:
  - <span class="pl-s">privacy</span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">This was really tough. I'm very interested in your feedback, but the plugin should at least solve the font hosting problem once and for all. I've investigated and it seems that we only need <code class="notranslate">*.woff2</code>, since this covers the whole range of browsers that we are <a href="https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/browser-support/" rel="nofollow">officially supporting</a>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Of course, it's still possible to achieve self-hosting manually without the use of the plugin, which I described in my last comment. The cool thing is that the plugin will download all assets regardless of where they are defined – in the template, as additional JavaScript or style sheets, or in Markdown – when they're external, they're downloaded.</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap"><div class="ReactionPopoverAnchor__B84pko"><button data-component="Button" type="button" <p dir="auto">If anyone wishes to self-host – here's a great site that helps download a customized version for your target languages: <a href="https://google-webfonts-helper.herokuapp.com/fonts/roboto" rel="nofollow">https://google-webfonts-helper.herokuapp.com/fonts/roboto</a></p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Select the character sets you really need</li>
<li>Select styles 300, 400, 400i and 700</li>
<li>Copy the CSS and <a href="https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/changing-the-fonts/#additional-fonts" rel="nofollow">add it in an additional stylesheet</a></li>
<li>Download the fonts and put them in your <code class="notranslate">docs_dir</code> relative to the CSS file</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Repeat for the monospaced font with the weights you need (probably 400 and 700)</p>
<p dir="auto"><del>Sadly, this is a manual process and not automatable. Again, if we would automate it, we would either need to determine the necessary charsets (very complicated) or bundle all charsets (too big, your Lighthouse score might suffer).</del> Turns out it is automatable, albeit it was quite tough. See my next comment.</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">For me, this still sends a request to google, see <a href="https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/blob/master/material/base.html#L57">https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/blob/master/material/base.html#L57</a></p>
<p dir="auto">only by using</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>mkdocs.yaml</strong></p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-yaml notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="...
theme:
  font: false
..."><pre class="notranslate">...
<span class="pl-ent">theme</span>:
  <span class="pl-ent">font</span>: <span class="pl-c1">false</span>
...</pre></div>
<p dir="auto"><strong>extra.css</strong></p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-css notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=":root > * {
  --md-text-font:"Roboto";
  --md-code-font:"Roboto Mono"
}"><pre class="notranslate"><span class="pl-kos">:</span><span class="pl-c1">root</span> <span class="pl-c1">></span> <span class="pl-ent"><span class="pl-c1">*</span></span> <span class="pl-kos">{</span>
  <span class="pl-c1">--md-text-font</span><span class="pl-kos">:</span><span class="pl-s">"Roboto"</span><span class="pl-kos">;</span>
  <span class="pl-c1">--md-code-font</span><span class="pl-kos">:</span><span class="pl-s">"Roboto Mono"</span>
<span class="pl-kos">}</span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">It works and there are zero outgoing connections.</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1
